symptom: Same-run Go repair could mutate one file but could not plan compiler-proven equivalent declarations across package files, causing repeated verifier failures.
root_cause: The registry covered only one diagnostic spelling and the planner only handled generated intra-file lines. It could neither parse all compiler pairs from one receipt nor locate equivalent cross-file functions, methods, structs, variables, and declaration groups. A second span bug let single-line var declarations consume a later brace and overlap.
repair_strategy: Bind primary, companion, and method-already-declared diagnostics to one runtime source tool; parse every compiler-located pair in one receipt; emit precise primary-only text replacements only for same-directory, same-package, build-tag-free, token-equivalent complete declarations; reject semantic differences.
forbidden_actions: semantic choice between different function bodies

verification.live_workspace_shadow_wave_1: two patches removed initial type/function/var/const duplicates without touching source workspace
verification.live_workspace_shadow_wave_2: two patches removed equivalent methods/functions; residual narrowed to non-equivalent Engine.Step, undefined applyPhysics, unused imports, and Bubble.Validate

next_action: Restart only the isolated L3-22 backend onto current Polaris code, retry the failed quality boundary without PM/CE replay, then require authoritative effect receipts and go test revalidation.
